about.title: About Faro Marina
paragraphs: Faro Marina is the waterfront area located in the historic center of Faro, Algarve.
It sits next to Praça Dom Francisco Gomes, connecting the old town with the Ria Formosa lagoon.
It is a starting point for boat trips and a peaceful place for seaside walks.
about.managedBy: Managed by Docapesca – Portos e Lotas, S.A. (Portuguese ports & fish-market authority) together with the Câmara Municipal de Faro (Faro City Council).

history.title: History & Maritime Heritage
history.intro: From an ancient trading port to the maritime gateway of the Algarve.
history.historicalSignificance: A sheltered Moorish-origin harbour, raised to the Algarve's maritime centre after the 1755 earthquake and regional capital since 1756.
paragraphs: The history of Faro Marina (Doca de Faro) goes back to the Moorish period, when Faro was known as Santa Maria de Faaron. As a natural sheltered harbour at the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula, it was an important trade hub for salt, olive oil, figs and dried fish with the Mediterranean and North Africa.

The 1755 Lisbon earthquake and the ensuing tsunami destroyed much of the Algarve coastline. However, thanks to the natural barrier-island protection of the Ria Formosa lagoon, the marina and old town suffered less direct impact. In 1756, Faro replaced the heavily damaged Silves and Lagos as the capital of the Algarve, and the marina became the region's political and economic maritime hub.

During the Age of Discovery, the marina was a stopover for explorers and merchant ships. Today mostly yachts and sailboats moor here, yet the water's topology still preserves the historical layout rebuilt in the 18th century.

ecology.title: Natural Heritage: Ria Formosa Lagoon
ecology.intro: The land gateway to the Ria Formosa Natural Park.
paragraphs: Faro Marina is not just a human mooring point — it is the land gateway to the Ria Formosa Natural Park. The site was designated a natural park in 1987 and was voted one of the 'Seven Natural Wonders of Portugal'.
The lagoon is formed by 5 barrier islands and 2 peninsulas. Two daily tides bring rich nutrients, creating a unique salt-marsh ecosystem.
The waters host seahorses (Hippocampus guttulatus and Hippocampus hippocampus), threatened species. The seagrass beds are an ideal nursery for them.
During spring and autumn migrations, over 20,000 waterbirds rest here, including flamingos, the purple swamphen (the park's emblem) and spoonbills.

legends.title: Legends & Architecture
legends.intro: The stories and design behind the landmarks near the marina.

items.title: Arco da Vila & the enlightened bishop
items.text: Near the marina, the Arco da Vila is Faro's most representative neoclassical building. It was designed by Italian architect Francisco Xavier Fabri in 1812 at the invitation of the enlightened bishop D. Francisco Gomes de Avelar. A niche on its façade houses St. Thomas Aquinas, the patron saint of Faro.

items.title: The legend of the Enchanted Moorish Princess
items.text: Legend says that on the eve of 1249, a Moorish princess hid her family's treasure in the wells and waters by the old walls. On St. John's Eve, visitors boating the marina may sometimes hear the distant singing of the young Moorish maiden from deep in the marsh.

practical.title: Practical Info & Public Amenities
practical.intro: A guide to public services and facilities around Faro Marina — maintained in a neutral, independent way, without recommending any specific brands or businesses.

groups.title: Restrooms & Public Utilities
items: Marina restrooms: near the marina square service area, with standard cubicles and an accessible WC (PRM accessible).
Old Town and park facilities: by Jardim Manuel Bivar and the Arco da Vila gate.
Usage tip: some public restrooms may require small coins (0.50–1.00 EUR) or a scan-to-pay code; carry change. All public areas have step-free access.

groups.title: Parking & Vehicle Access
items: Blue Zone (time-limited parking): along the marina and side streets, with roadside meters where you buy and display a ticket.
Open-air public car parks: large areas on the marina outskirts and by the railway line, suited to long stays.
Underground car park: near the Old Town entrance, covered and cooler, charged by the hour.
Drop-off zone: short-stay bays at the marina entrance, for taxis and passenger pick-up/drop-off only.

groups.title: Fuel & EV Charging
items: Public EV charging (MOBI.E network): in the outer marina car parks and along main roads, with 11/22 kW AC and rapid charging, payable by card or app.
Fuel stations: along the N125 and towards Faro Airport, with Gasolina 95/98, Gasóleo and self-service wash/air.

groups.title: Supermarkets, Shops & Supplies
items: Municipal Market (Mercado Municipal): on the Old Town edge, best for fresh fruit, seafood, olive oil and local produce.
Neighbourhood minimarkets / supermarkets: around the marina and nearby streets, for water, snacks and sunscreen.
Pharmacy (Farmácia): on the Old Town shopping street and main junctions, marked with a green cross, for over-the-counter medicine and basics.

groups.title: Dining & Meal Times
items: Marina-view snack-bar / café: for coffee, Pastel de Nata and light salads by day, with harbour views.
Traditional tavern / restaurante típico: in the Old Town alleys, with grilled fish, Cataplana and home-style dishes.
Meal-time tip: lunch 12:30–15:00, dinner 19:30–22:30; some taverns close between 15:00 and 19:00.

groups.title: Accommodation Areas & Types
items: Marina-view hotels & apartments: next to the Marina, with open waterfront views and easy ferry access.
Old Town B&B / guest house: inside or around the walls, in old buildings — cultural feel, but cobbled streets are tricky for large luggage.
Hostel & budget stays: between the train station and the marina, for backpackers and independent travellers.

transport.title: How To Get There
transport.intro: Faro Marina sits in the city centre, a short walk from the train station and the main bus terminal. Here are the practical ways to reach it.

modes.title: By Air — Faro Airport (FAO)
modes.body: Faro Airport is about 7–10 km west of the marina. From arrivals you can take the city bus (Próximo line 16) to the Terminal Rodoviário in roughly 25–35 minutes; taxis and app-based rideshares take around 15 minutes. All major car-rental companies have desks at the airport.
tips: City bus line 16: pay on board for a few euros; frequency drops in the evening and at weekends.
Taxi or rideshare to the centre: typically €10–18, depending on time of day and luggage.
Rental cars: compare the desks at the airport and book ahead in summer.

modes.title: Public Transport — Bus, Train & Coach
modes.body: Faro's urban buses (Próximo) link the airport, station, beach and suburbs; buy a ticket on board. The railway station is a key stop on the Algarve line, with regional trains to Lagos and Vila Real de Santo António and fast services to Lisbon. The Terminal Rodoviário offers national and international coach connections.
tips: Urban bus fare: around €1.80–2.00; a reloadable card is cheaper for several trips.
Train to Lisbon: Alfa Pendular in about 3 hours — book early for the best fare.
Coaches: long-distance and cross-border services leave from the Terminal Rodoviário, opposite the marina.

modes.title: Taxi & Rideshare
modes.body: Taxi ranks sit at the airport, the train station and near the marina entrance. App-based rideshares also operate in Faro and are usually priced similarly. Both are convenient with luggage or for late arrivals.
tips: Use the marked ranks or the official apps; for taxis, confirm a rough fare if no meter is shown.
From the station to the marina it is a very short ride — walking is often quicker.

modes.title: By Car & Parking
modes.body: Navigate to Praça Dom Francisco Gomes, 8000-168 Faro. The marina is well signed from the A22 / IC4. From Lisbon take the A2 then the A22 (about 2.5–3 hours); from Spain follow the A22 / AP-7. Several public parking areas and a short-stay drop-off zone are within a few minutes' walk.
tips: Blue Zone time-limited parking by the marina; open-air car parks and an underground car park near the Old Town for longer stays.
In peak season spaces fill up — arrive early or use public transport.

modes.title: On Foot from the Station
modes.body: Faro railway station and the Terminal Rodoviário are both within walking distance. Exit the station and follow Av. da República southeast for about 500 m (6–8 minutes) to reach the marina; the bus terminal is directly opposite the marina entrance, a walk of under 3 minutes.
tips: The route is flat and step-free — an easy stroll along the avenue.
Wheeled luggage is fine; cobbled streets begin only inside the Old Town.

items.a: It is at Praça Dom Francisco Gomes, in the center of Faro, Algarve.
The waterfront is public and free to access; boat trips are paid.

items.q: What is the best time to visit?
items.a: Spring and autumn offer pleasant temperatures.

items.q: How to get from the airport?
items.a: You can take a taxi, bus or rental car from Faro Airport (FAO), about 10 km away.

items.q: Is parking easy near the Marina?
items.a: There is a Blue Zone time-limited area by the marina, open-air car parks and an underground car park near the Old Town. In peak season spaces fill up — arrive early or use public transport.

items.q: Do public restrooms charge a fee?
items.a: Some public restrooms may require small coins (0.50–1.00 EUR) or a scan-to-pay code. Carry change; all public areas have step-free access.

items.q: Are there EV charging points nearby?
items.a: Yes, on the public MOBI.E network, in the outer marina car parks and along main roads, with 11/22 kW AC and rapid charging, payable by card or app.

items.q: What public facilities are near the Marina?
items.a: Public restrooms, car parks (Blue Zone and underground), EV charging on the MOBI.E network and transit hubs are all within a short walk — see the map section for exact spots.

seasonal.title: Seasonal Travel Strategy
seasonal.intro: A quarter-by-quarter guide to Faro Marina and the Ria Formosa — combining typical weather, sea conditions and wildlife so you can plan around nature, not just the calendar.

rows.weather: Mild 16–22°C, light rain easing, gentle breezes — the most comfortable walking season.
rows.water: Sea 16–18°C and mostly calm; island ferries run regularly.
rows.wildlife: Peak of flamingos and migratory birds; wildflowers along the lagoon edge.

rows.weather: Hot 28–35°C, almost no rain, very strong UV at midday — plan outdoor time for morning and evening.
rows.water: Sea 20–24°C, warmest and busiest; lifeguards on the ocean beaches only.
rows.wildlife: Fewer migratory birds, but juvenile fish and sea turtles are active; boat trips are at their best.

rows.weather: Warm 22–28°C, sea still warm, far fewer crowds — many consider this the ideal window.
rows.water: Sea ~22°C; calm, clear water good for swimming and photography.
rows.wildlife: Birds begin returning; soft light and peaceful lagoons.

rows.weather: Mild 12–18°C but wetter, with the occasional Atlantic storm and dramatic skies.
rows.water: Sea 15–17°C — cool, for the hardy; some ferry services are reduced.
rows.wildlife: Wintering flamingos and waders fill the lagoon; the quietest, cheapest season for the city.

itineraries.title: Recommended Itineraries
itineraries.intro: Pick a route that matches your group and pace. All start at Faro Marina.

audiences.title: Families with children
audiences.body: Short, flat and low-stress: waterfront views, a playground, a gentle boat ride and time for ice cream — without long hikes.
steps: Seaside walk along the marina promenade
Play and rest at Jardim Manuel Bivar
Short boat trip to the nearest barrier-island beach
Ice cream and an early dinner before the afternoon heat

audiences.title: Photography & nature
audiences.body: Built around light and wildlife: sunrise and sunset at the water, a lagoon boat trip, and the textures of the old town.
steps: Sunrise over the Ria Formosa from the marina
Boat trip into the lagoon for flamingos and seabirds
Old-town alleys, Arco da Vila and the cathedral
Causeway or ferry to Ilha Deserta / Barreta for open horizons

audiences.title: Low-effort / accessible
audiences.body: Mostly step-free and unhurried: a waterside café, benches, and a short taxi or boat hop, skipping long island walks.
steps: Flat promenade walk with frequent benches
Short taxi or adapted boat to an accessible beach
Leisurely return through the Old Town

routes.title: Half-day (2–3 h)
routes.body: A compact loop of the waterfront and the historic centre.
items: Faro Marina and Praça Dom Francisco Gomes
Arco da Vila and the Old Town
Faro Cathedral and a café stop
Back along the waterfront

routes.title: Full-day (5–6 h)
routes.body: The half-day loop plus a lagoon island experience.
items: Morning: marina, Old Town and cathedral
Midday: lunch by the water
Afternoon: boat trip to Ilha Deserta, Barreta or Culatra
Late: beach or picnic, then sunset on the way back

responsibility.title: Science & Visitor Responsibility
responsibility.intro: Faro Marina is the land gateway to the Ria Formosa Natural Park. A little awareness goes a long way in keeping it healthy.

science.title: A nursery of the Atlantic
science.text: The lagoon's seagrass meadows and salt marshes are a breeding ground for fish and the protected long-snouted seahorse.

science.title: A stopover for 20,000+ birds
science.text: Twice a year, tens of thousands of waterbirds rest and feed here, including flamingos and the purple swamphen, the park's emblem.

science.title: A protected coastline
science.text: Created in 1987 and voted among Portugal's natural wonders, the barrier islands shield Faro from storms and erosion.

duty: Take all litter with you — bins are limited on the water and the islands.
Keep your distance from birds and never feed wildlife.
Use reef-safe sunscreen and avoid stepping on seagrass beds.
Choose licensed, low-impact boat tours that follow the park's rules.
Respect seasonal no-entry zones that protect nesting and spawning.
